pois.name: Administration Office
pois.blurb: The association office: POA business, stamps, faxes and copies, key fobs, RV registration, and the recreation “Ticketron” desk for every WLE event. Building Compliance is at the side entrance. Public Safety calls are handled here too.

pois.name: Main Club House · Indoor Pool & Gym
pois.blurb: Indoor pool with changing rooms, showers, saunas and lifeguards, the Main Club House hall (137 seats, kitchen) where most WLE events happen, and the gym — the Fitness Center, open around the clock with a key fob.
facts: Water aerobics 8:15 · laps 9:30 · open swim 10:30 – noon
24 hours, 7 days · key fob and signed waiver from the office · 12 and up

pois.name: Rockledge Pool & Snack Shack
pois.blurb: The main outdoor pool, with a diving board, the Snack Shack, sand volleyball, a sandbox, BBQs and a large picnic area. The bocce courts are on the rise just above the pool. Palm Park and a school bus stop are here too.
facts: Open during pool hours · hot and cold food

pois.name: Bocce Courts
pois.blurb: Two bocce lanes on the rise above Rockledge Pool, a short walk up from the pool gate.
facts: Uphill from Rockledge Pool, on the south-west side

pois.name: Adult Lodge
pois.blurb: A lodge for adults (21+) with pool tables, TV, books, couches and a kitchen, beside Rockledge Pool and the sand volleyball court. Home of the Thursday breakfast and the monthly Recreation meeting.
facts: 6:30 AM – 2:00 AM with a key fob

pois.name: Kasper Lodge & Skate Park
pois.blurb: Ed Smith Field: the kids' game room at Kasper Lodge — video games, pool tables, ping pong, foosball and TV — with the playground, skateboard park, golf nets and playing field right outside. Maintenance and the compactor are here too.
facts: Open until dusk · ID and parental waiver required

pois.name: Beaver Pool & Lodge
pois.blurb: 25-metre outdoor pool with a kiddie pool, diving board, showers, picnic area and the Snack Shack. Home of the swim team in late June and July. Beaver Lodge next door hosts WLE events, owner parties and teen hours.

pois.name: Beaver Courts · Pickleball
pois.blurb: The courts behind Beaver Pool: pickleball-only open play. Everyone is welcome — be helpful to beginners, and keep to an hour when people are waiting.
facts: Mon, Tue, Thu · 5 PM to dusk
Open play, first come first served

pois.name: Game Courts at Tennis Lane
pois.blurb: Tennis and basketball courts, plus handball, horseshoes and a picnic area. The gate side is open for tennis and pickleball; the basketball side is tennis only. Open daily, first come first played.
pois.photoCredit: Rob Schilling · the courts and Deer Lake from the air, September

pois.name: Ballfield
pois.blurb: The baseball field and its parking area, with a playground beside it. Open 9 AM to dusk. The official WLE map also shows the dog park and the leaves-and-branches drop-off right next to it.

pois.name: Deer Beach
pois.blurb: Sand beach on Deer Lake with restrooms and water fountains. No lifeguards — swim at your own risk.
facts: Registered non-power boats only · off the racks by the first Saturday of November
pois.photoCredit: Rob Schilling · Deer Lake and its beach, September

pois.name: Beaver Beach
pois.blurb: Sand beach on Beaver Lake with restrooms, water fountains, a picnic area with grills and tables, and a playground. No lifeguards — swim at your own risk.
facts: Registered non-power boats only · off the racks by the first Saturday of November

pois.name: Beaver Lake Dock · Small Boats
pois.blurb: The dock and small boat access at the north end of Beaver Lake. Racks for registered non-power boats, first come first served. Register at the office (January to early April, $50); boats can go out from the first Saturday of April and must be off by the first Saturday of November.

pois.name: WLE Marina
pois.blurb: The community's private marina on Lake Wallenpaupack. Slips are assigned from a waiting list — the wait for a permanent slip can run 7–8 years.

pois.name: Main Entrance · Mailboxes
pois.blurb: The main entrance, with the mailboxes and parcel lockers across the parking lot from the Administration Office, and a school bus stop. USPS asks everyone to wait behind the rope while the carrier is loading the boxes.

pois.name: West Entrance · Mailboxes
pois.blurb: The west entrance off Luzerne-Wayne Turnpike, with mailboxes, parcel lockers and a school bus stop. It is the entrance nearest Lakeland Drive and Indian Drive. USPS asks everyone to wait behind the rope while the carrier is loading the boxes.

pois.name: 9/11 Memorial
pois.blurb: The Wallenpaupack Lake Estates 9/11 Memorial on Marina Drive, near the Administration Office.

pois.name: Recycling & Sewer Plant
pois.blurb: The community's water and sewage facility, where Indian Drive, Beaver Lake Drive and Tomahawk Road meet. Recycling drop-off is here.
facts: Mon–Fri 8 AM – 4:30 PM · Sat 9 AM – 2:30 PM

pois.name: Deer Lake Dam
pois.blurb: The dam that holds Deer Lake.
pois.photoCredit: Rob Schilling · Deer Lake under ice, March

pois.name: Beaver Lake Dam
pois.blurb: The dam that holds Beaver Lake, completed in 1974.

pois.name: Craft Shop & Laundromat
pois.blurb: The WLE Clothing & Craft Shop and the community laundromat, between the office and Ed Smith Field.

pois.name: Main Beach & U-Dock
pois.blurb: The beach on Lake Wallenpaupack — the Big Lake — below the Main Club House, with a picnic area and the U-Dock.
pois.photoCredit: Rob Schilling · the Estates shoreline on Lake Wallenpaupack, February

pois.name: Beaver Lake Small Boats
pois.blurb: Small boat access on Beaver Lake, just north of the beach. Racks for registered non-power boats, first come first served. Register at the office (January to early April, $50); boats can go out from the first Saturday of April and must be off by the first Saturday of November.

pois.name: Genese Park · Small Boats
pois.blurb: Genese Park at the north tip of Deer Lake, with small boat access. Racks for registered non-power boats, first come first served. Register at the office (January to early April, $50); boats can go out from the first Saturday of April and must be off by the first Saturday of November.

pois.name: Deer Lake Small Boats
pois.blurb: Small boat access and the T-dock at the south end of Deer Lake, off Mohican Road. Racks for registered non-power boats, first come first served. Register at the office (January to early April, $50); boats can go out from the first Saturday of April and must be off by the first Saturday of November.
pois.photoCredit: Rob Schilling · Deer Lake under ice, March

pois.name: Fish Hatchery
pois.blurb: The fish hatchery pond beside Deer Lake.

pois.name: Campgrounds
pois.blurb: The members-only campground at the end of Red Lawn Lane, in the south-west corner of the Estates: 22 sites, four of them for tents and the rest with water and electric for trailers and motor homes, plus restrooms, showers and a small playground.

pois.name: Lacawac Sanctuary trails
pois.blurb: The nearest real hiking: a nature preserve just south of the Estates with more than nine miles of marked trails around Lake Lacawac and down to Lake Wallenpaupack. This pin sits on the edge of the map — tap Directions for the trailhead on Sanctuary Road.
facts: Lake Lacawac Trail (1.1 mi, moderate) · Big Lake Trail (2.9 mi, harder)
